phase3_findings.description: The PR's own transient changeset .changeset/issue-1745-brand-devflow-buckets.md (1 brand-cased DevFlow, classified pending) is recorded as a pending_sweep_baseline row in lib/test/brand-devflow-buckets.json. On merge to main the version-consolidate workflow deletes consumed changesets, so the file vanishes from the pending set and the lint's reverse-direction stale-row check fires (cmd_check lines 191-197 -> 'stale pending_sweep_baseline row'), returning rc=1. ci.yml runs on push to main, so the consolidation commit's own 'lib + python tests' required check goes RED, and every subsequent PR branched from main inherits the stale row until someone manually reseeds. Self-inflicted post-merge breakage of the merge-gating check. Verified directly: the row is present at line 41 and the changeset carries exactly 1 DevFlow.

Corroborates the code-reviewer finding: the issue-specific changeset recorded in pending_sweep_baseline is deleted by version-consolidate on merge, firing the reverse-direction stale-row check and turning lib + python tests RED on main. Agent simulated the deletion and confirmed the stale row. Fix: exclude transient .changeset/*.md issue files from the reconciled population (keep permanent README.md), or reword the changeset to carry no brand-cased DevFlow.

The bucket-record read-error path (main() lines 250-254, return 2 on OSError/JSONDecodeError) is entirely untested by the #1745 run.sh block; the --buckets flag is never exercised either. If it silently regressed to return 0 the whole reconciliation would pass vacuously. A one-line test invoking --buckets /nonexistent.json asserting rc=2 would close it.

Behavior-inert-prose-capped (Phase 4.1.5): the module docstring (line 25 'in --check mode', line 46 'Modes: --check (default)') presents --check as an accepted flag, but argparse defines only --root/--buckets/--update-baseline/--print-population; passing literal --check errors 'unrecognized arguments'. The default reconcile path takes no flag. The '(default)' qualifier mitigates but the flag-shaped formatting is inaccurate. run.sh comments carry the same '--check green' wording. Docstring in internal-only lib/test tooling (pruned from vendor slice, no external consumer, no tool parses it for behavior) -> both inertness limbs hold -> capped at Suggestion, does not drive REJECT. Remedy: describe it as the default/no-flag reconcile mode in all three sites.

repo_root() cwd fallback (lines 77-89) can fail open in the gating --check mode: an unresolved git toplevel degrades to Path.cwd() with only a stderr breadcrumb; if that tree has no unclassified occurrences cmd_check returns 0 (green gate off the wrong/empty root). Low risk in-suite (always runs inside the repo). Consider treating an unresolved toplevel as a finding on the gating path, or requiring --root.

Count-based forward guard (line 184, count != recorded) has an inherent blind spot: a sweep that removes one prose DevFlow and adds a new one in the same file keeps count == recorded and passes unflagged. Acceptable for a rename-residue backstop but the docstring/changeset present the guard as catching 'a new occurrence' without noting the limitation; one sentence would prevent over-trust.

cmd_check summary line 'audited {audited} of {audited} files' (line 208) prints the same variable twice, so the 'N of N' ratio is always trivially equal; skipped files are not counted in audited. Drop the redundant 'of N' or compute a real tracked total.

--print-population argparse help (lines 244-245) says 'a provenance file emits both a pending and a frozen line', but cmd_print_population emits the pending line only when pcount > 0; a provenance file with no renameable remainder emits only the frozen line. The docstring's own wording (lines 50-52) is precise; the help drops the qualifier.

Test-coverage gaps on secondary classify branches and defensive paths: frozen-tooling branch (lines 134-135) never isolated by the fixture (tooling_files is []); frozen-record/frozen-historical only negatively asserted (no positive --print-population bucket-identity assertion); repo_root cwd-fallback (80-89) untested; --update-baseline/--print-population breadcrumb-and-continue-on-skip path untested. Core reconciliation logic is directly covered; these are secondary/error paths.

report: Shadow review (iteration 3, blinded) of PR #1973 (issue #1745). Full expected roster dispatched (5 reviewers, all returned; type-design-analyzer correctly gated OFF — no new types). VERDICT: REJECT. The verdict is driven by a corroborated (2 agents: code-reviewer Critical, requesting-code-review Important) correctness defect: the PR records its own transient changeset .changeset/issue-1745-brand-devflow-buckets.md as a pending_sweep_baseline row, but version-consolidate deletes consumed changesets on merge to main, which fires the lint's reverse-direction stale-row check (return rc=1) and turns the required 'lib + python tests' check RED on main's own push CI immediately after merge, blocking every subsequent PR until the baseline is manually reseeded. Verified directly (row at line 41; changeset carries 1 DevFlow). This is a self-inflicted post-merge breakage of the merge-gating check — graded Critical, drives REJECT at the default critical threshold; it is a spurious fail-open (false RED on main), not a suite-RED-at-desk over-grade, so no 4.1.5 cap applies. Fix: exclude transient .changeset/*.md issue files from the reconciled pending population (keep permanent .changeset/README.md), or reword the changeset to carry no brand-cased DevFlow. Secondary: an untested return-2 bucket-record read-error path (Important test_gap); several Suggestion-level items (--check documented as an accepted argparse flag — capped inert; repo_root cwd fail-open; count-based blind spot; 'audited N of N'; --print-population help overstatement; assorted secondary test gaps). Acceptance criteria otherwise look satisfied on the real tree (lint rc=0, ~1120 files audited, ruff clean; AC1/AC3/AC4 mechanism sound, AC5 executable pins add no prose pins, AC6 no skills/agents bodies touched). The mechanism is well-built and merge-ready once the changeset-baseline defect is fixed.
